sections.html:
Hutchinson is the Reno County seat, in south-central Kansas where U.S. 50 meets K-96, about 39 miles northwest of Wichita. It lies on the northeast bank of the Arkansas River, and Cow Creek, a tributary, runs southeast through town. The city covers 22.69 square miles of land, enough room for older streets near downtown, newer blocks toward the edges and industrial ground along the rail lines.

The July 1, 2025 estimate is 39,595 residents, a 1.0 percent drop from the April 2020 base of 40,007. The city has lost people slowly since 2010, when the count was 42,080. Households stay put: 80.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and median household income is $58,687.

sections.h2: Salt City history and old brine wells
sections.html:
C.C. Hutchinson founded the town in 1871 under a deal with the Santa Fe Railway. In 1887, Ben Blanchard drilled for oil nearby and found salt, and Hutchinson became Salt City. The Carey Salt Company opened the only salt mine in the city in 1923, the Hutchinson Salt Company runs it today, and Cargill and Morton Salt operate evaporative plants. Dillon's and Kwik Shop headquarters, a hydraulics plant, an agricultural equipment maker and a regional hospital round out local employment.

One piece of history reaches individual parcels. On January 17, 2001, natural gas leaked from the Yaggy storage field, traveled underground and surfaced through old brine wells. A downtown explosion destroyed two businesses and damaged 26 others, and a second blast the next day killed two people in a mobile home park. If a buyer asks, your title company and the county can help pull the records for your parcel.

With 2.22 people per household and 17.5 percent of residents at 65 or older, one- and two-person households are common. Older owners who are downsizing, and the heirs of those owners, make up a good share of sellers. Home values are modest, so the gap between a repair bill and the house's worth can be narrow.

sections.h2: How does Hutchinson's weather affect a house?
sections.html:
Summers are hot and humid, winters cold and dry. Temperatures top 90 degrees on about 63.4 afternoons a year and fall below freezing on about 119.5 mornings. Precipitation averages 32.93 inches, and May is the wettest month. Hutchinson reached 113 degrees on July 27, 2011, and fell to minus 19 on February 16, 2021, the coldest reading on record.

  • A hard freeze like the one in February 2021 threatens exposed plumbing, crawl spaces and older water heaters.
  • Hot summers wear on roofing and on air conditioners that are 15 or more years old.
  • Cow Creek and the Arkansas River run through the area, so ask the county or city about floodplain status before telling a buyer a property sits outside it.

Ordinance 2019-17 requires every residential rental unit in the city to hold a rental license, renewed each year. A unit without one by the May 31 deadline is in violation, an administration fee of $20 a month applies for each month it is rented without a license, and operating an unlicensed unit is a Class C misdemeanor.

The ordinance also sets up a voluntary interior inspection program. Landlords or tenants can ask the Inspections Department for an inspection, and results are posted on the city's website. Units in good standing that pass can earn best-practice rental status, which cuts the license fee by 50 percent for three calendar years.

Selling a rental house? Confirm the license is current before closing so the buyer does not inherit a fee or a violation. Check the city's website for the current ordinance text, since the rules can be amended.

Three public districts serve the area: Hutchinson USD 308, Nickerson-South Hutchinson USD 309 and Buhler USD 313. USD 308 runs eight elementary schools, two middle schools, Hutchinson High School and a career and technical academy.

  • U.S. 50 runs east-west south of the city, K-96 bypasses it on the west, and K-61 crosses the east side.
  • Reno County Area Transit runs three bus routes, called Red, Blue and Yellow.
  • Amtrak's Southwest Chief stops here, and Wichita's airport handles most commercial flights.

The mean commute is 15.6 minutes. Because Wichita is 39 miles away, some buyers commute there, and easy access to U.S. 50 or K-96 helps a house.

The Reno County Appraiser, Register of Deeds and Treasurer all work from 125 W. 1st Avenue in downtown Hutchinson, so a recorded deed, a tax question and a parcel record can often be sorted out in one trip during closing week.

  • Tax calendar. The treasurer mails statements on or after November 1. The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by May 10, and a variable interest penalty accrues after that.
  • Protests. An owner who has not appealed before can file a protest form with the treasurer by December 20, or by January 31 if a lender pays the tax from escrow.
  • Deeds. Most deeds need a sales validation questionnaire under K.S.A. 79-1437c. Recording fees follow state law, K.S.A. 28-115, and depend on page count.

Unpaid taxes are paid from your sale proceeds at closing, so back taxes do not block a sale. The county says a residential property has three years to redeem after unpaid tax begins running, or it can be sold at tax foreclosure auction, usually in the fall.

Tell the buyer and the title company about any back taxes at the start, and ask how the balance will be handled at closing. Do not wait for the redemption period to run down.

sections.h2: What do Hutchinson sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Common situations include a house that needs a lot of work relative to its value, a rental with a tenant, an estate, and a move to be near family.

  • Older homes. Houses near downtown may have older wiring, plumbing and roofs.
  • Rental license issues. A lapsed license adds monthly fees.
  • Inherited property. Heirs may live far away and want to stop paying taxes and utilities on an empty house.
  • A smaller buyer pool. A financed buyer's appraisal can flag repairs the lender will not fund.

A cash buyer can price the house as it stands and close at a Reno County title company on your schedule. Get the offer in writing and compare it with listing costs and time on the market.

faqs.q: How many people live in Hutchinson, KS?
faqs.a: An estimated 39,595 residents as of July 1, 2025, down slowly from 42,080 at the 2010 census.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Reno County?
faqs.a: The Reno County Register of Deeds sets fees under state law (K.S.A. 28-115), and the amount depends on the number of pages. Call the office at 125 W. 1st Avenue or ask your title company to quote the fee before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rental house in Hutchinson?
faqs.a: The license is required to rent the unit, not to sell it. The city charges $20 a month for each month an unlicensed unit is rented after the May 31 deadline, so bring the license current before closing.

faqs.q: When are Reno County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half of real estate tax is due by December 20 and the second half by May 10. Statements go out on or after November 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hutchinson house that has unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing. Unpaid real estate tax can lead to tax foreclosure and auction after a redemption period, which is three years for residential property, so do not wait.
